title: ShockAssessment
description: Shape contract for the shock-category reasoning pass. Two echoed findings, then the category they imply, then the justification for it. The input is a closed physical-examination payload rather than a document, so unlike every other contract in this pack nothing here is copied out of prose.

x-notes.propertyOrder: LOAD-BEARING, as everywhere in this pack. The two primary findings are echoed FIRST because on this contract the echo is the reasoning: the published rule is a lookup on skin temperature and jugular venous pressure, so a model that has just written both down has everything the category requires. shock_category follows immediately. The two justification arrays follow the category rather than preceding it, because 'which findings support this' is a question about an answer that must already exist -- asking for support first is asking the model to assemble evidence before it has a claim, which is how a rationalisation gets written down as a reason. assessment_confidence sits near the END for the reason it does in vital-signs.schema.json: a confidence demanded before the commitment has been measured to turn one case into eight thousand characters of padding.
x-notes.indeterminateIsAMember: `indeterminate` is a member of the shock_category enum rather than the property being nullable. A model that cannot decline from inside the grammar will not decline; on a closed enum of three named diseases the alternative to declining is a coin flip between them. Abstention has to be sayable before it can be measured, and it is measured in both directions -- see abstentionRecall and overAbstention in src/profiles/clinical/shock.ts. Two of this contract's cases exist only to test it: the 2x2's unassigned fourth cell, and a payload whose jugular venous pressure was not assessable.
x-notes.enumsHereAndNotInVitalSigns: vital-signs.schema.json argues that `unit` must NOT be an enum, because an enum makes a unit error impossible to emit and therefore impossible to measure. That argument does not carry here and the difference is the input. A unit is the model's rendering of prose that could say anything; these findings are echoes of a payload whose vocabulary is closed and known before the request is sent. The measurable error is picking the wrong member -- reading `cool` as `warm` -- and an enum does not hide that, it isolates it. A free string would instead let the model answer `coolish` and make echo fidelity unscoreable, which is the failure the enum argument is trying to prevent, arriving from the other side.
x-notes.arrayBounds: maxItems and uniqueItems on both arrays, and they are load-bearing rather than decorative. A grammar blocks EOS while an array is open, so an unbounded array is a run that cannot stop -- see the README. Five is the number of findings the payload contains, so a citation list longer than five is already citing something twice or something absent. uniqueItems keeps a model that has run out of things to say from filling the array by repeating its best finding.
x-notes.findingNamesAreAnEnum: supporting_findings and discordant_findings hold FINDING NAMES, not free prose, and this is what makes the invention check exact. On the extraction contracts a quote is checked against a document by literal containment, and the check has to be careful because a document is long and a span may be legitimately reformatted. Here the payload is closed: a name outside this enum is a finding nobody obtained, with no relaxation under which it might be there. The grammar cannot emit one at all, which means the check in scoreReply catches the case that matters instead -- a name that IS in the enum but is `not_assessed` in this payload. That is the more dangerous error, because the finding sounds real and a reader will not query it.
x-notes.reasonIsFreeText: indeterminate_reason is a string rather than an enum of the three reasons `classify` can give. The rule's reasons are closed; the model's are not, and a model that declined for a reason the rule has no word for should be able to say so -- that sentence is the most useful thing this contract can produce and an enum would delete it. It is consequently NOT graded automatically, which is stated here so nobody reads its presence as a checked field.
x-notes.numericBounds: minimum/maximum on assessment_confidence are documentation and validator input; llama.cpp's json-schema-to-grammar does not enforce numeric ranges in GBNF.
